Finding: US 11,132,920 B2 (IBM): "Personalized intervention based on machine learning of behavior change states". Maps interventions to a behaviour-change process model with a feedback learning loop; "framework agnostic"
Relevance / impact for our project: Closest conceptual overlap with our orchestrator. Low risk for an academic prototype. Before commercialising: FTO check of its claims. Document our HAPA + BCIO hierarchy as distinct

Finding: US 2019/0103189: "Augmenting eHealth interventions with learning and adaptation capabilities". Q-function estimates the long-term value of an action in a user state, starting from a prior intervention
Relevance / impact for our project: Overlaps with "learn on top of an expert-designed intervention". Same action as P1

Finding: US 11,653,878 B2 (Pivot/Carrot): quantification and prediction of smoking behaviour (CO sensor-based)
Relevance / impact for our project: Only relevant if we add CO-sensor-based prediction. Keep CO as optional self-report input
Hardware; we do not build sensors. No impact unless we partner with a sensor vendor

Finding: In Europe, programs for computers "as such" are excluded from patents (EPC Art. 52(2)(c), (3)). Software is patentable only with a further technical effect
Relevance / impact for our project: Patenting our own method is unrealistic and not needed. Protect our work through copyright plus an open licence or a university agreement

Finding: Copyright protects expressions, not ideas, procedures or methods (TRIPS Art. 9(2))
Relevance / impact for our project: We may implement ACT, CBT, MI and BCTs freely, but must write our own texts, audio and exercises rather than copy iCanQuit, Smoke Free or manuals

Finding: BCIO ontologies (incl. BCTO, setting, mode of delivery) published on GitHub under CC BY 4.0; OWL on BioPortal (2,524 classes, version 2025-06-13)
Relevance / impact for our project: We can embed the ontology at runtime and in explanations, with attribution. Main legal enabler for the BCT-coded catalogue

Finding: BCTTv1 labels and definitions were published in a Springer article (Michie et al., 2013). We did not find an explicit open licence for the taxonomy text; the papers on its successor (BCTO) are CC BY 4.0
Reference: Michie et al. (2013); Marques et al. (2023)
Relevance / impact for our project: Use BCTO / BCIO identifiers as the machine-readable source. Check the BCT Taxonomy site terms before shipping BCTTv1 definitions in the app

Finding: Validated questionnaires are copyrighted texts. FTND is widely reproduced, but we found no public-domain statement; some hosts offer it only under their own licence
Reference: Heatherton et al. (1991); NIDA DataShare; Millisecond
Relevance / impact for our project: Intake chatbot: list every instrument (FTND/HSI, HAPA scales, motivation-to-stop) with its licence. Ask the authors if unclear. Keep items verbatim only if allowed

Finding: Open-source licences of reusable platforms: RADAR-base (Apache 2.0), mindLAMP (BSD-3), Rasa Open Source (Apache 2.0, maintenance mode); m-Path is proprietary
Reference: Ranjan et al. (2019); mindLAMP docs; Rasa docs
Relevance / impact for our project: Permissive licences allow reuse in an app we might release. Avoid copyleft surprises: keep a licence register in the repo

Finding: Rasa Pro Developer Edition: free, including in production, up to 1,000 conversations per month
Relevance / impact for our project: Enough for a prototype and small user study. A paid licence is needed at scale

Finding: LLM providers' terms: API use is subject to usage policies (e.g. restrictions on medical advice without safeguards); open-weight models come with model licences (e.g. Llama community licence with an acceptable-use policy)
Relevance / impact for our project: Pick a provider with EU data processing and a DPA. Log which model version produced each chatbot message

Finding: Registered trademarks exist for competitor names (e.g. "QuitBot", "Smoke Free", "Quit Genius")
Relevance / impact for our project: Choose a distinct app name. Run a TMview check before branding the prototype

Finding: EU MDR + MDCG 2019-11 rev.1 (2025): qualification depends on the manufacturer's intended purpose. Lifestyle and wellbeing tracking is not medical device software; software for diagnosis, therapy or prevention of disease is. Rule 11 typically gives class IIa or higher
Relevance / impact for our project: Project: wellbeing / research prototype wording, no treatment claims. After the project: a DiGA-style route would require CE marking as class IIa, a QMS (ISO 13485) and clinical evidence

Finding: Belgium: FAMHP supervises health apps that are medical devices. mHealthBelgium pyramid: M1 = CE mark, M2 = security and interoperability, M3 = socio-economic evidence → reimbursement. No smoking app is at M3
Relevance / impact for our project: Shows the long-term path to reimbursement in Belgium; not in scope for the project

Finding: GDPR Art. 9: health data (wearable data, EMA on cravings and smoking) is a special category. Consumer apps generally rely on explicit consent, which must be separate from accepting the terms. Location can reveal health status by inference
Reference: GDPR Art. 9, 7, 35; EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent
Relevance / impact for our project: Separate opt-in per data source (fits our modular design); data minimisation; a DPIA for the user study; EU hosting

Finding: EU AI Act Art. 50: users must be told they are interacting with an AI system; applicable from 2 Aug 2026. AI in an MDR device that needs a notified body is high-risk (Art. 6(1)); those obligations are delayed to 2028 under the Digital Omnibus (verify)
Reference: AI Act (EU) 2024/1689; MDCG 2025-6; commentary (Hunton, Pure Global)
Relevance / impact for our project: The chatbot must disclose that it is an AI. As long as we are not a device, we are not high-risk. Our explanation layer anticipates AI Act transparency expectations

Finding: Google Health API (replaces the Fitbit Web API): all scopes are "Restricted" and need a privacy and security review. Apple App Review 5.1.3 restricts how HealthKit data may be used (no advertising, no data mining)
Reference: Google Health API docs; Apple App Review Guidelines 5.1.3
Relevance / impact for our project: Factor review time into the plan. Prefer on-device Health Connect / HealthKit reads for the prototype

Finding: Ownership of student project results: depends on UGent rules and any partner agreement (e.g. with the Health Psychology Lab)
Relevance / impact for our project: Agree early on who owns the code and content and under which licence it is released
